CommonJS and ESM binding relationships were recovered from inert syntax and resolved only within the inventoried artifact container.
Configuration extraction covers process.env, process.argv, node:fs reads, and direct logical defaults.

Resource extraction covers built-in filesystem/network acquisition and exact local close/destroy/end handles.

observations.name: notebook-runtime-final
limitations: Artifact identity is unavailable for this observation.
Event sequence records provider receipt order; simultaneous browser causality is not inferred.
Network content is retained only when selected; Playwright response-body bytes are API results and are not guaranteed to match wire bytes.
Request bytes are limited to what Playwright exposes; not_exposed does not establish body absence or multipart file coverage.
Network content reads settle within 5 seconds each and the observer does not request bodies from unfinished responses.

Captured response-body bytes are the result of Playwright's Response.body() API. Playwright may satisfy that API with a credentialed follow-up load of the request URL when CDP has no body, so transaction and event links do not verify that retained bytes came from the original network transaction.
Playwright scenario events do not expose request initiator stacks; receipt order does not prove causality.
Storage values are hashed only after declared-secret redaction.
Some selected network content was unavailable; per-transaction content states retain the reason.
Browser host platform and architecture were not observed.
